## TL;DR

Completed a desktop browser QA pass on Agents, Checks, Settings, and Releases using the auth-less server from this task worktree. All four routes loaded, the safe navigation and refresh/preview/copy interactions worked, and the browser recorded no page errors, console errors, or failed requests. No reproducible defects were found, so no product code or test changes were needed. Findings are recorded in `docs/qa/2026-11-web-desktop-pages.md`.

## Work and rationale

I confirmed the current worktree and active task, then started the app with `just serve-noauth 7272` as the task requires. The local server bound to `127.0.0.1:7272` and identified itself as RepoOS 0.5.89 on Bun 1.4.4. CUA reported that its browser access host was unavailable; the native Chrome instance also could not connect to the runner's loopback address. Because Playwright Chromium was installed in the runner and could reach the same local server, I used that browser at a 1440 × 1000 desktop viewport to complete the app-side interactions and collect console/page errors and failed requests.

Each target route returned HTTP 200. I exercised all nine Agents section controls, all four Checks tabs, and all seven Settings tabs. Checks and Settings exposed their tabs with accessible tab semantics, and each clicked tab reported selected. I used the Checks and Releases refresh controls, opened the Releases email preview and verified its content appeared, and clicked one release-channel Copy action. The checks page refresh completed. These interactions produced no captured page errors, console errors, or failed network requests. Detailed coverage is in the QA record.

I did not invoke model tests or agent editing because they can run external providers or persist configuration. I did not create or publish a release, send release email, or perform import/export. The generation/publish flow already covered by #1168 was intentionally skipped. The main goal here was to look for desktop regressions in page rendering and ordinary navigation/read-only controls, while avoiding persistent or external actions that were outside the QA scope.

No defect reproduced during the pass, so adding code changes or tests would not be justified. I created the requested QA findings document and left this report draft for RepoOS to finalize against the checked tree.

`REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed. Because the branch changes only documentation, RepoOS classified it as bookkeeping-only: format, lockfile sync, zero-runtime-dependency, branch-artifact, task-asset, and task-parser steps passed; build, tests, and UI smoke were correctly skipped for this diff. The check reported no failed steps.

## Approaches tried

- Checked the assigned branch, worktree, task state, and handoff status.
- Started the requested auth-less worktree server and first attempted to reach it from the computer-use Chrome. That browser is isolated from the runner's loopback network, so it returned `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`.
- Launched the repository-installed Playwright Chromium in the runner and drove the same server at desktop width. Verified all four routes and all listed navigation tabs, then used safe refresh, preview, and copy controls.
- Captured page errors, console errors, and failed requests during the browser pass; all three collections were empty.
- Ran the required changed-path RepoOS check once; it passed with documentation-only steps skipped as described above.

## Challenges and blockers

The computer-use browser host could not connect to the runner-local server, and CUA's browser inventory was unavailable. This prevented inspection in the user's native Chrome window. It did not block the QA task: in-runner Chromium accessed the server directly and allowed route and interaction testing at the required desktop viewport. The QA record notes this environment boundary so the evidence is clear.

The task asks for every control to work, but some controls execute provider calls or make persistent/external changes. I limited interactions to section navigation and read-only or locally scoped actions, and documented the excluded controls. The specifically excluded #1157 and #1168 scenarios were not repeated.

## Key learnings

For this setup, `127.0.0.1` refers to the runner from the Playwright process but not from the separate computer-use Chrome host. The local browser fallback can still exercise the worktree server and record JavaScript and request failures, but it is not evidence of what the user's installed Chrome window rendered. Future QA needing native Chrome should use a browser bridge that shares the runner's host or expose an explicitly supported preview connection.

The four routes rendered and the navigation structure remained functional at desktop width. No test was added because no regression was observed; the task's existing automated gate remains the check for integration safety after the QA document change.
